doc.title: Benny Waters interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995

title: Being the senior member of the Statesmen of Jazz
summary: He praises the Statesmen idea but would want more rehearsal for recordings, and says many great players are over 65.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Tell us about how it felt to get the phone call to be one of the “Statesmen of Jazz.”
Tell us about how it felt when you were called to be one of the members of the “Statesmen of Jazz” — the senior member.

Well I thought it was a great thing, see? And I still think it’s a great thing in the regards that if I’m playing in it or who, I think the idea is great and I wish it a big success. But I think, I think that if we’re going to record, I think we could have made more stress on getting a perfect record, and to do that you have to have rehearsals. See that’s my only complaint, see? But the idea is great. Because you have thousands and thousands of guys 65 and over that play well. You may not have many 93 year olds, because they’re not living. See but 65 and 70, you know, oh between 65 to 80 for instance, there’s thousands of guys that, I’ll tell you the truth, for my part, some of the best musicians who are playing jazz are over 65. The type of jazz I like, you know?
